targetTexts.1: A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
targetTexts.2: It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.
targetTexts.3: Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.
targetTexts.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
targetTexts.5: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.
targetTexts.6: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.
targetTexts.7: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
targetTexts.8: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.
targetTexts.9: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.
targetTexts.10: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.
targetTexts.11: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.
targetTexts.12: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
targetTexts.13: Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?
targetTexts.14: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.
targetTexts.15: In my futile life I have seen both of these: A righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.
targetTexts.16: Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
targetTexts.17: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
targetTexts.18: It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.
targetTexts.19: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.
targetTexts.20: Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
targetTexts.21: Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
targetTexts.22: For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.
targetTexts.23: All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.
targetTexts.24: What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?
targetTexts.25: I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.
targetTexts.26: And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.
targetTexts.27: “Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.
targetTexts.28: While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.
targetTexts.29: Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made mankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
